asked: why cant i just add 1/2 + 1/3 = 2/5? my teacher says its wrong

doubt.subject: Adding fractions with different denominators
doubt.question: Why is 1/2 + 1/3 = 2/5 wrong and what is the correct answer?

steps.title: Tops and bottoms mean different things
steps.detail: The top number tells how many pieces you have. The bottom number tells how big each piece is. Halves are bigger than fifths, so you cannot just add tops and bottoms.

steps.title: See it with a treat
steps.detail: Imagine you have 1/2 of a chocolate bar plus 1/3 of another same bar. Just the 1/2 alone is already bigger than 2/5. So the answer must be bigger than 1/2, and 2/5 cannot be right.

steps.title: Make the pieces the same size
steps.detail: To add, we cut both into the same tiny size pieces. 1/2 = 3/6 and 1/3 = 2/6. Now both are counted in sixths.

steps.title: Now add
steps.detail: Now add the pieces: 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6. That is almost a whole bar. So 1/2 + 1/3 = 5/6.

doubt.key_idea: Make the pieces the same size first, then add.
doubt.misconception: Many students add tops together and bottoms together, but the bottom tells the size of the piece, so adding bottoms changes the size and gives a wrong tiny answer.

check_questions.q: What is 1/3 + 1/2? Hint: change to sixths first.
